members.name: standardConformingStrings
members.doc: The PostgreSQL `standard_conforming_strings` session parameter. Set to `false` to not set the option. WARNING: Setting this to false may expose vulnerabilities and is not recommended!

members.name: clientMinMessages
members.doc: The PostgreSQL `client_min_messages` session parameter. Set to `false` to not override the database's default.

members.name: hooks
members.doc: Sets global permanent hooks.

members.name: minifyAliases
members.doc: Set to `true` to automatically minify aliases generated by sequelize. Mostly useful to circumvent the POSTGRES alias limit of 64 characters.

members.name: logQueryParameters
members.doc: Set to `true` to show bind parameters in log.

members.name: schema
members.doc: If defined the connection will use the provided schema instead of the default ("public").

members.name: attributeBehavior
members.doc: Sequelize had to introduce a breaking change to fix vulnerability CVE-2023-22578. This option allows you to revert to the old behavior (unsafe-legacy), or to opt in to the new behavior (escape). The d

members.name: logging
members.doc: A function that gets executed while running the query to log the sql.

members.name: benchmark
members.doc: Pass query execution time in milliseconds as second argument to logging function (options.logging).

members.name: modelName
members.doc: Set name of the model. By default its same as Class name.

members.name: version
members.doc: Enable optimistic locking. When enabled, sequelize will add a version count attribute to the model and throw an OptimisticLockingError error when stale instances are saved. Set to true or a string wit

members.name: defaultScope
members.doc: Define the default search scope to use for this model. Scopes have the same form as the options passed to find / findAll.

members.name: scopes
members.doc: More scopes, defined in the same way as defaultScope above. See `Model.scope` for more information about how scopes are defined, and what you can do with them

members.name: omitNull
members.doc: Don't persits null values. This means that all columns with null values will not be saved.

members.name: timestamps
members.doc: Adds createdAt and updatedAt timestamps to the model. Default true.

members.name: paranoid
members.doc: Calling destroy will not delete the model, but instead set a deletedAt timestamp if this is true. Needs timestamps=true to work. Default false.

members.name: underscored
members.doc: Converts all camelCased columns to underscored if true. Default false.

members.name: hasTrigger
members.doc: Indicates if the model's table has a trigger associated with it. Default false.

members.name: freezeTableName
members.doc: If freezeTableName is true, sequelize will not try to alter the DAO name to get the table name. Otherwise, the dao name will be pluralized. Default false.

members.name: name
members.doc: An object with two attributes, `singular` and `plural`, which are used when this model is associated to others.

members.name: indexes
members.doc: Indexes for the provided database table

members.name: createdAt
members.doc: Override the name of the createdAt column if a string is provided, or disable it if false. Timestamps must be true. Not affected by underscored setting.

members.name: deletedAt
members.doc: Override the name of the deletedAt column if a string is provided, or disable it if false. Timestamps must be true. Not affected by underscored setting.

members.name: updatedAt
members.doc: Override the name of the updatedAt column if a string is provided, or disable it if false. Timestamps must be true. Not affected by underscored setting.

members.name: engine
members.doc: You can also change the database engine, e.g. to MyISAM. InnoDB is the default.

members.name: comment
members.doc: Finaly you can specify a comment for the table in MySQL and PG

members.name: initialAutoIncrement
members.doc: Set the initial AUTO_INCREMENT value for the table in MySQL.

members.name: hooks
members.doc: An object of hook function that are called before and after certain lifecycle events. See Hooks for more information about hook functions and their signatures. Each property can either be a function,

members.name: validate

members.name: setterMethods
members.doc: Allows defining additional setters that will be available on model instances.

members.name: getterMethods
members.doc: Allows defining additional getters that will be available on model instances.

declarations.doc: Sets validation options for annotated field

declarations.doc: Adds options be assigning new options to old one

declarations.doc: Determines models from value

declarations.name: getScopeOptions
declarations.doc: Returns scope option meta data from specified target

declarations.name: getSequelizeTypeByDesignType
declarations.doc: Maps design types to sequelize data types;

declarations.name: inferDataType
declarations.doc: Infers sequelize data type by design type

declarations.name: installHooks
declarations.doc: Installs hooks on the specified models

declarations.name: prepareOptions
declarations.doc: Prepares sequelize config passed to original sequelize constructor

declarations.doc: Resolves all model getters of specified options object recursively. So that {model: () => Person} will be converted to {model: Person}

declarations.doc: Resolves scopes and adds them to the specified models

declarations.doc: Sets seuqlize define options to class prototype

declarations.doc: Dummy database file, which gets required by sequelize, to make validation of models possible without using the actual ORM or any database connection.
